about: Made by scripts/make_replica_vectors.py; checked by scripts/check_replica.py and web/scripts/check-replica.mjs.

cases.what: a log's changes are applied, and it has caught up to the head
a change with a bad signature is left out, the rest applied
a change signed as a snapshot is left out (the prefix is part of what's signed)
a snapshot is applied
a snapshot signed for another position is left out
a change that doesn't decrypt is left out, the rest applied
a compressed change is applied
something that isn't a change is left out, the rest applied
a malformed entry is left out, the rest applied
a change from a revoked personal link, stored before it was revoked, is applied
a log in pages: caught up only after the last
a page that comes without a log first is ignored
changes out of order: caught up only as far as nothing is missing
an acknowledgement counts as received
the server lost its copy (its log ends before ours): caught up to its head
the server lost its copy (we're at or below what it dropped): caught up to its head
an editor whose server lost the copy sends the whole document again
it remembers the newest change it has from the server, and says so on reconnecting
not a snapshot, which the server replaces: the newest change before it
the server's log isn't the one it last saw: caught up from the start, remembering the new log
an editor whose server's log isn't the one it last saw sends the whole document again
a project that's only relayed: nothing is lost, and it stays caught up where it was
an editor replaces a long log with a snapshot
a read-only link doesn't make snapshots
a short log isn't replaced
a project that's only relayed has no log to replace
no snapshot while a change's upload is missing (it would leave the change out)
a change kept as an upload is fetched and applied
a change whose upload is gone: catch up again from the start
a change whose upload can't be fetched just now: caught up only to just before it
an upload that isn't what the change names counts as gone
a revocation signed by the owner is kept
a revocation arriving on its own is kept
a revocation not signed by the owner is ignored
a deletion signed by the owner: the project is deleted here
a deletion not signed by the owner is ignored
a server that turns away old apps: refused, with the version it needs
a log clears an earlier refusal
the server not storing changes is remembered, and cleared once one is stored
the server saying it only relays the project clears a storage problem
a project that's only relayed needs no creation code
the owner's signed storage setting is followed
a storage setting not signed by the owner is ignored
an older signed storage setting put back by an editor doesn't count
an older signed storage setting doesn't count even when both come in one catch-up
a newer signed storage setting is followed
a signed change from a peer is applied once caught up
a compressed change from a peer is applied
a change from a peer before catching up is ignored (revocations aren't in yet)
an unsigned change from a peer is ignored
a change from a peer signed by a revoked personal link is ignored
a change from a peer signed by another project's key is ignored
a change from a peer in pieces is put together and applied
a peer's message that doesn't decrypt is ignored
an editor answers a peer that just connected: its state, and what the peer lacks
a read-only link sends a peer its state, but no changes (it can't sign them)
a peer that already has everything is sent nothing more
an edit is sent, and kept until the server acknowledges it
an edit made while catching up waits, and goes once caught up
several edits waiting go as one change
an edit not acknowledged is sent again after reconnecting
an acknowledged edit isn't sent again after reconnecting
an acknowledged edit counts as the newest change it has from the server
an edit the server won't store is kept, and the reason shown
an edit and a change from someone else both end up in the document
a file added here is uploaded, signed, as a project file
compiled output is uploaded marked as output
a file added while catching up is uploaded once caught up
a file the server won't store is kept to try again, and the reason shown
a file the server can't take just now is kept to try again
a file stored again clears a storage problem
a project that's only relayed uploads no files (they go peer to peer)
a read-only link uploads nothing
a file is fetched from the server
a file the server swapped for other content isn't taken: peers are asked instead
a file the server doesn't have is asked of peers, and a peer's answer taken
a peer's answer with other content than asked for is ignored
a file kept here is given to a peer that asks for it
a peer asking for a file not kept here gets nothing
